offers with `proposeCommand`, one at a time. Three SDKs carry it; this file
is the one answer all three are held to, so the question a test answers is
not "does Rust still do what Rust did" but "do the three agree".

portable_schema.rs::LOCAL_FIELDS — the daemon drops them anyway; the helper

how_to_read_this.accepted: `text` is the exact file text; the helper must return exactly `commands`, in order (member order is not significant).
how_to_read_this.refused: `text` is the exact file text; the helper must fail, and its error message must contain `mentions`.
how_to_read_this.local_fields: the members removed from every command, top level only — each SDK's own list must EQUAL this one.
how_to_read_this.unsafe_integers: numbers Rust and Python read exactly and a JavaScript number cannot: Rust and Python must return `commands`; TypeScript must refuse with an error containing `ts_mentions`, never round.

accepted.name: commands-file
accepted.note: What Astra's Export writes: `source_id` and `enabled` on every command, the provenance members null. Only TOP-LEVEL local members go: an `id` inside an action is the action's own.

commands.name: Good morning
commands.description: Reads the news when you say good morning

accepted.name: group-file
accepted.note: A group export, hand-edited to carry every local member a command has in Astra: all of them dropped, an unknown member kept for the daemon to judge.

accepted.name: empty
accepted.note: A file with no commands is a file, and offers nothing.

accepted.name: a-later-version
accepted.note: `version` is a number, as the format declares it; which number is not the helper's business — the daemon reads every command it is offered.

accepted.name: graph-mode
accepted.note: A graph-mode command — `editor_mode` and `workflow` — travels whole; ids INSIDE the workflow are the graph's own, not local members.

accepted.name: duplicate-members
accepted.note: A member given twice collapses to the LAST one in all three SDKs (serde_json, Python's json and JSON.parse agree). The daemon's strict reader would have refused the duplicate; the helper re-serialises, so what is offered is the last value alone.

accepted.name: proto-member
accepted.note: A top-level `__proto__` member is an ordinary key: kept as data, never a prototype (TypeScript builds the command with Object.fromEntries).

refused.name: one-portable-command
refused.note: One command on its own is what `proposeCommand` takes, not a .astra file.

refused.name: legacy-single-command
refused.note: The pre-group `astra-command` format; Astra still imports it, the helper does not read it.

refused.name: number-overflow
refused.note: 1e400 is no finite number: serde_json refuses it, and Python and TypeScript refuse it rather than read infinity.
